equity_bridge.item: Expected Respironics DOJ / State AG resolution (probability-weighted, unprovisioned)
equity_bridge.note: Excluded from 2026 outlook and 2026-2028 targets (Q2 2026 6-K line 113). Analyst judgment, not a company figure: the consent decree is in place and PI/economic-loss claims are settled; the residual DOJ civil/criminal and 41-state AG matters are unquantified.
FY2025 20-F balance sheet; associate income is outside Adjusted EBITDA, so the asset is added here (matching-asset rule).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management 2026-2028 mid-single-digit comparable sales CAGR, tempered for FX and Philips' record of missing mid-term targets; equity CAGR rejected (Respironics charges and buybacks, negative).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.6% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (+0.6% 5y) and EPS; all historical series are distorted by the 2021-2025 Respironics recall (provisions, settlements, US deferred-tax de-recognition in FY2024). FY2022 owner FCF was negative so 3y FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (no equity-award tax line; interest income not stripped, net debt). FY2020 1,523 -> FY2025 371 = -24.6% 5y CAGR vs -20.7% reported; the gap is SBC rising from EUR 112m to 141m against a recall-depressed FY2025 FCF base, not a structural shift to stock pay (SBC <1% of sales).

scenario_narratives.base: Philips executes roughly two-thirds of its 2026-2028 plan: comparable sales grow ~4% as imaging (Diagnosis & Treatment) and Image Guided Therapy hold share and Personal Health grows high single digits, offset by a still-weak China and slow recovery of the US sleep & respiratory franchise under the consent decree. The EUR 1.5bn productivity programme roughly offsets cost inflation and tariffs, taking Adjusted EBITA to ~14% (vs the 'mid-teens' target) once the 2026 tariff refund drops out. Restructuring and quality charges shrink to ~1.5% of sales but never disappear. The DOJ/State AG matters settle for an amount in the hundreds of millions.
scenario_narratives.bull: Philips finally hits a mid-term plan: mid-single-digit comparable growth from AI-enabled imaging, IGT devices and Personal Health; Respironics re-enters the US sleep market under the consent decree; productivity lands in full and Adjusted EBITA reaches the mid-teens by 2028 and ~16% thereafter, closing part of the gap to Siemens Healthineers and GE HealthCare. DOJ resolution is modest and buybacks resume at scale.
scenario_narratives.bear: Quality and compliance remain the binding constraint: another field action or FDA escalation, a large DOJ/41-state AG settlement or criminal resolution, continued China volume-based-procurement price cuts and anti-corruption drag, and US tariffs that productivity cannot offset. Comparable growth runs ~2%, Adjusted EBITA stalls around 12%, and the market keeps valuing Philips as a structurally sub-par medtech.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Philips on normalized owner free cash flow, not on recall-distorted reported years. The core businesses generate ~EUR 1.4-1.6bn of FCF a year on management's definition; the question is whether margins move from ~12% to mid-teens Adjusted EBITA, and how much of the Respironics tail is still to be paid. SBC is small (<1% of sales) so the house/street band is narrow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Unquantified DOJ / 41 State AG Respironics resolution (EUR 600m expected value in the bridge; could be multiples of that)
Repeat quality / FDA enforcement action in any segment
China volume-based procurement and anti-corruption campaign pressure on imaging
US tariffs: 2026 includes a one-off ~EUR 0.2bn refund that does not repeat
USD weakness: ~1/3 of sales in North America, translated into EUR
Execution: Philips has repeatedly missed mid-term margin targets

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 23.70-33.44; PHIA.AS and EURUSD=X same API for the parity check
data_sources.financials: PHG_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, EUR millions); FY2025 20-F (cash flow statement, balance sheet, lease maturity table); Q2 2026 6-K (net debt composition, FCF composition, diluted shares, outlook); Q4 2025 6-K (2026-2028 mid-term targets)
data_sources.qualitative: Company filings and info.json business summary; PHG_Analysis.json was not yet available at build time

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average, Q2 2026 6-K (968,574 thousand). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; Philips is a repurchaser (EUR 411m FY2024, EUR 68m Q2 2026 plus EUR 353m of share-repurchase forwards carried in debt), so the flat count is funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based compensation' add-back EUR 141m. Philips settles awards from treasury shares; no separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis). Interest income (EUR 85m) NOT stripped: the company is in net debt, so there is no cash pile double-count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks nil (paused while Respironics settlements were paid); FY2024 EUR 411m; Q2 2026 EUR 68m resumed.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in EUR; NYSE PHG quote in USD. PHG is a New York Registry Share, 1:1 with the Euronext ordinary share (no ADS ratio). EUR->USD 1.1257 = Yahoo EURUSD=X at 2026-10-02T21:29Z. Parity check: PHIA.AS EUR 21.27 (2026-10-02 close) x 1.1257 = USD 23.94 vs PHG USD 23.92 -- 0.1% tie, confirming the rate, direction and 1:1 basis. Per-share values computed in EUR and converted; unsuffixed values are USD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR build: Bund 10y ~2.7% + ERP 5.5% x beta ~1.0 = cost of equity ~8.2%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.4% (weighted bond coupon, Q2 2026 6-K) -> ~2.5% after tax; D/V ~22% at market -> ~6.9%. Rounded up to 7.5% for all three scenarios. Litigation/quality risk is charged in the flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) leases as operating cost: lease cash (~EUR 241m next-year minimum payments, principal + interest, FY2025 20-F lease maturity table) deducted as lease_cost_pct 1.35% of revenue; lease liabilities (EUR 953m at 2026-06-30) EXCLUDED from debt (total debt 7,464 - 953 = 6,511); D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation so cash-tax EBIT is not double-charged.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI EUR 29m equity / ~EUR 1-3m income per year -- immaterial, ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year (FY2026-FY2035), scenario-weighted, with the non-US adaptations (EUR WACC, EUR/USD bridge, single lease treatment). Philips is a diversified health-technology manufacturer (Diagnosis & Treatment, Connected Care, Personal Health) -- an operating company whose value is a FCF stream; no bank/REIT/holdco feature applies. NORMALIZATION: reported FY2025 FCF of EUR 512m is depressed by the EUR 1,025m Respironics medical-monitoring and personal-injury settlement payment (H1 2025); FY2022 (-961) and FY2024 also carry recall outflows. Normalized FY2025 street FCF ~EUR 1.54bn (512 + 1,025), house owner FCF ~1.40bn before lease principal. The forward build is anchored to the component margins and to management's FY2026 FCF guidance (EUR 1.5-1.7bn incl. a one-off ~EUR 0.2bn US tariff refund) and 2026-2028 cumulative FCF target (EUR 4.5-5.0bn), not to the distorted reported year. Historical median reported FCF FY2015-FY2025 is EUR 906m but that series is pre-IFRS-16 before 2019 and recall-distorted after 2021. EBITDA margin path = Philips Adjusted EBITDA + SBC (Adjusted EBITDA is after SBC) LESS a recurring charge for restructuring, quality actions and Respironics running costs (FY2025 'restructuring, acquisition-related and other items' were EUR 531m, 3.0% of sales; modelled at ~2.5% in FY2026 fading to ~1.5%), because Philips has booked these every year for a decade. CapEx is net capex incl. capitalized development and purchased intangibles (3.7% of sales FY2025); D&A excludes ROU depreciation and acquired-intangible amortization is treated as tax-deductible within D&A. Working capital capture negative (manufacturer, receivables+inventory > payables+contract liabilities). DOJ / State AG Respironics investigation is excluded from all company guidance; an expected-value EUR 600m deduction sits in the equity bridge. Model and route chosen fresh (no prior memory entry).

bear.margin_note: FY2027-28 dip carries an incremental ~EUR 0.5bn of DOJ/AG resolution and remediation cost over the bridge's expected value, plus China volume-based procurement and tariff pressure.

base.growth_note: FY2026 reported -1%: comparable +3-4.5% guided but H1 reported sales -2% on USD translation. FY2027-28 ~4-4.5% vs management's mid-single-digit comp target; fades to 2.5%.
base.margin_note: FY2026 16.0% = Adjusted EBITDA ~18.5% (13.75% EBITA guide midpoint incl ~1pp tariff refund + ~4.8pp D&A) + 0.9% SBC - ~2.5% restructuring/quality/Respironics running costs - ~0.9% for provision cash usage and WC outflow so year-1 owner FCF ties to guidance (~EUR 1.45bn house unlevered ex-lease vs 1.6bn guided levered street). FY2027 flat as the refund drops out and productivity offsets; mature 17.8% equals ~14% Adjusted EBITA after 1.5% recurring charges -- below the 'mid-teens 2028' target, reflecting Philips' history of missing targets. Base 2026-28 cumulative FCF on management's basis ~EUR 4.8bn, inside the 4.5-5.0bn target range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: an open, unquantified DOJ/State AG investigation, a US consent decree constraining Respironics, and a decade-long record of quality failures and missed mid-term targets. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things (target delivery, Respironics US re-entry, benign DOJ outcome, China recovery) to go right together. Base 50% is management's plan partially delivered.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
